promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, race week, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week, Oct 5 – 11, went to plan on every day, and your marathon-pace work at about 8:36 per mile sits right on the under-3:45 pace. The week of Oct 12 – 18 is race week, so the job is to arrive fresh: short sharpening, no extra long run, and a controlled start on Sun Oct 18.

answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer:
No, skip the 16-miler.

A run that long, four days out, adds fatigue you will not recover from by Sunday.

Your fitness is already built, and the 20-miler on Sun Oct 4 showed that. Keep Wednesday to the short session in the plan.

You are not losing fitness. A week of lower volume does not undo weeks of training, and your easy pace and heart rate have held steady for four weeks. Flat, heavy legs are the usual feeling of a taper, and they should lift within a few days.

new.analysis:
## What last week showed
Last week, Oct 5 – 11, matched the plan on every day. All five runs and both rest days were done as written, for about 34 miles in total. Nothing was skipped and nothing was overrun, so the week gives a clean read on how the block is landing.

The most useful number is the marathon-pace work on Wed Oct 7. The planned four miles at marathon pace ran at about 8:36 per mile with no fade, which is the pace the under-3:45 goal needs. The table sets that session beside your other runs.

| Session | Pace per mile | Average heart rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marathon-pace work, Wed Oct 7 | 8:36 | 147 bpm |
| Easy runs, Tue and Thu | 9:51 to 9:52 | 139 bpm |
| Long run, Sun Oct 11 | 10:00 | 146 bpm |

Your easy runs have held the same pace and heart rate for four weeks, so the aerobic base is steady. The heavy, flat legs after the 12-mile long run are the fatigue of a big block, and they should lift as the volume falls.

## Why race week looks like this
Race week should cut volume while keeping some faster running. The plan falls to about 18 miles before the race, which is well under half of your 46-mile peak week. That is the right direction for a marathon taper.

The one quality session, on Wed Oct 14, is kept short on purpose. Two miles at marathon pace keep the rhythm familiar without leaving fatigue for Sunday. The strides on Tue, Thu and Sat keep your legs quick without adding load.

## How to run the race
Under 3:45 means averaging about 8:35 per mile or faster on Sun Oct 18. Your long runs show steady splits with no fast finish, so a controlled start is worth more than an early push. The table lays out how to pace the day.

| Miles | Pace per mile | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 to 6 | about 8:45 | Settle in and save legs for later |
| 7 to 20 | 8:30 to 8:35 | Hold goal pace steadily |
| 21 to 26.2 | 8:30 or faster | Only if the effort still feels controlled |
